title: telemetry-correlation-graph-and-instant-playbook-drafts
author: Maya Chen
description:
Add a telemetry correlation graph service and an 'instant playbook' generator for on-call responders. Motivation: when incidents spike we frequently need to assemble a short, accurate runbook and identify cross-service signal that correlates with the incident in the first 3–5 minutes. This PR introduces a lightweight correlation graph that links traces, metric anomalies, and recent deploys, plus a templated playbook-drafter that synthesizes the top 3 remediation steps and quick debug commands for Slack/WarRoom consumption.

Goals and scope: produce an initial MVP that runs as a sidecar in incident-bot, emits a correlation-graph artifact to the incident context, and exposes a /playbook-preview endpoint for the UI and Slack actions. This is intentionally conservative: we do not auto-execute any actions, only surface suggestions and confidence scores.

Checklist:
- [x] core correlation engine (time-windowed anomaly join + dependency heuristics)
- [x] playbook drafting templates with guardrails and provenance headers
- [x] REST endpoint and Slack action integration
- [x] unit and integration tests for deterministic parts of the pipeline
- [x] docs + troubleshooting notes in incident-bot/README.md

Related work: Linear ENG-1892 (incident automation backlog), follow-up to ENG-1204 (on-call context snapshots). May touch SRE runbook ownership; added runtime flag to opt-out for clusters that prefer canonical runbooks.

Usage notes: a new incident annotation `correlation.graph=true` triggers the sidecar to produce a small graph stored on the incident object; the UI shows a compact visualization and a 'Draft Playbook' button that returns a 3-item, ranked action list with confidence. The playbook generator includes exact commands (kubectl/jq/psql) where known, plus a 'why' sentence and suggested rollback/hotfix steps if applicable.

Safety and privacy: the correlation graph keeps only obfuscated trace IDs and metric names by default; full identifiers require `incident_bot.debug.show_raw_ids` feature flag and explicit operator consent. No secrets or key material are collected or stored.

Why this is different: previous PRs suggested runbook recommendations but relied on static templates. This PR glues streaming telemetry signals to templates and surfaces causality hints (recent deploys, config changes, and anomaly co-occurrence), which helps first responders prioritize faster.

review_conversation: Arjun Patel: Nice approach to keep this as a sidecar — reduces blast radius. Two asks: make the confidence score schema explicit and ensure we cap the query window to 10m by default.
Maya Chen (author): Updated scoring schema and added a config param 'correlation.window_seconds' with default 600 (10m). See commit b4f7e20.
Riley Summers: Playbook templates look good. Please avoid actionable commands that assume a specific cluster context; prefer templated placeholders with examples.
Maya Chen (author): Switched to placeholders and added example expansion logic behind a feature flag. Added tests to assert placeholders are present when feature flag is off.
Sofia Martinez: Integration test flaky on CI — failing on CI container startup. Suggest mocking the telemetry client; also add a health endpoint for the sidecar.
